newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore sarong party girl hooks up to Web.
newsitem.headline: Singapore sarong party girl hooks up to Web.

text.p: Singapore's sultry sarong party girl (SPG) has gone high tech with her own World Wide Web homepage, the publishers of SPG books said on Monday.
SPGs are Asian women seeking husbands from among European, Australian or American expatriates, a phenomenon that has not completedly faded despite rising affluence in Southeast Asia.

Set up by Flame of the Forest Pte Ltd, publishers of "The Official Guide to the Sarong Party Girl" and other books on the subject, the SPG website scores about 50,000 hits a month and consists of pages like Homepage, Home Sexlife, PartyTime, and Malebox.
The homepage lists the criteria for subscribers to gain access to the rest of the SPG pages -- they must be over 18, white, have money, and drive a Porsche or a Mercedes-Benz.
Leading the site's user sessions are Americans, accounting for nearly 50 percent, followed by Singaporeans, Malaysians, Koreans, Canadians, and Japanese, the publishers said.
"Far-flung males visiting her website included 96 in Finland, 57 in Belgium and 52 in Chile," publisher Alex Chako told Reuters. Access to the pages is free.
